h1: The 8 Best Convection Toaster Ovens for Baking, Roasting and Air Frying, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Convection Toaster Ovens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 convection toaster ovens scored on fan design, air-fry modes, controls, footprint and value, from Breville to Nuwave.
summary: Breville's BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is the convection toaster oven to buy if you want one countertop appliance to replace most of your full-size oven. The Breville BOV860BSS is the slightly simpler air-fry sibling, the Breville BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro is the choice if you only want convection, and the Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven is the best fit for a smaller counter.
intro: Many shoppers assume convection and air fry are two different features and pay extra for both. They are not. A convection toaster oven moves hot air with a fan, and an air fry mode simply runs that fan harder with the heat concentrated near the food. The real difference between a good oven and a frustrating one is how evenly it holds temperature, how clearly its controls read, and whether the tray fits your usual pan.

This ranking sorts by cooking flexibility and control quality first, then by size and value. We reviewed eight ovens from their listings, looking at air-fry capability, convection function, power rating where stated and the price bracket. Where a listing gives no detail, we do not guess; we describe the role of the model and its place in the range.

products.name: Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: Breville's flagship countertop oven, with air fry added to a full smart-element convection range.
products.description:
The BOV900BSS is the top of Breville's Smart Oven line. It combines a convection fan, a dedicated air fry setting and Breville's smart element approach, which adjusts heat output through a cook rather than leaving elements on full.

It wins because it is the most complete answer to one question: can a countertop box do the work of a wall oven? Smart-element ovens tend to hold a set temperature more steadily than basic toaster ovens that cycle on and off, which matters for baking and for reheating pizza without leaving a soggy centre. The compromise is size and cost. This is a large appliance in the $200 to $500 bracket, and it needs clear space around it for heat to escape.

Buy it if you cook most weeknight meals at home and want one machine to carry the load. Skip it if you rarely use more than a toaster function.
pros: Built to replace a small oven
products.idealFor: Home cooks who want one oven for most meals.
products.skipIf: You only need toast and the occasional reheat.

products.name: Breville BOV860BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer
products.verdict: The same Breville smart-element approach with air fry, at a step below the flagship.
products.description:
The BOV860BSS is the Smart Oven Air Fryer in Breville's range, combining convection cooking with a dedicated air fry setting. It sits in the same $200 to $500 bracket as the Pro model above.

It ranks second because it offers a very similar result with less of the top model's range. For most households, the gap between the two will show up in finer settings and a few conveniences rather than in how the food comes out of the oven. What it keeps is the thing that sets Breville apart from cheaper rivals: steady temperature control and a reputation for parts that last. It gives up ground on size and extras to the BOV900BSS.

It is a strong buy if you want Breville quality and air fry without chasing the flagship. Skip it if you want every feature the top model carries.
pros: Breville heat control with air fry
products.idealFor: Buyers who want Breville quality and air fry.
products.skipIf: You want the top model's extra range.

products.name: Breville BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro
products.verdict: The classic convection Breville, without a dedicated air fry mode.
products.description:
The BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro is a convection toaster oven with Breville's smart element design. It lacks the dedicated air fry setting of the two models above, and sits in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It places third because air fry is the feature many buyers now expect. That said, convection alone does most of what people want from a countertop oven: roasting vegetables, baking cookies and crisping frozen foods. If you rarely make wings or fries, the missing mode costs little. The model has been a reference point for countertop ovens for years, so accessories and recipes are easy to find. Against the Ninja ovens below, you get steadier baking and a more refined control system.

Choose it if you want a serious oven and care little for air fry. Skip it if air frying is the reason you are shopping.
cons: Costs as much as air-fry rivals
products.idealFor: Bakers and roasters who skip air frying.
products.skipIf: Air fry is your main goal.

products.name: Ninja Foodi XL Pro Air Fry Oven
products.verdict: A flip-away air fry oven with a bigger body than the standard Ninja.
products.description:
The Foodi XL Pro is Ninja's larger air fry oven, sitting in the $200 to $500 bracket. It is built around air frying first, with convection and standard oven modes arriving from the same fan design.

It ranks fourth because it fries well but is less refined as a baking oven than the Breville units above. Ninja focuses on fast, high-heat cooking, so wings, fries and reheated pizza are the strengths. The tradeoff is that thin-wall designs tend to give less even heat when baking, so cakes and delicate pastries are where you notice. It also asks for more bench space than the basic Ninja.

It is a good buy for families who fry and reheat more than they bake. Skip it if precise baking matters.
cons: Needs a lot of counter space
products.idealFor: Families who air fry and reheat daily.

products.name: Ninja Digital Air Fry Countertop Oven
products.verdict: A simpler Ninja air fry oven in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
The Ninja Digital Air Fry Countertop Oven is the standard Ninja version, with air fry as its headline function in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Fifth place goes to it as the cheaper cousin of the XL Pro, and the saving shows in size and finish rather than in how it fries. It is a good fit for two to three people and a compact kitchen. Like other thin-bodied air fry ovens, it will run hotter on the outside of the cabinet, so leave breathing room above and behind. Against the Cuisinart it offers Ninja's fast cooking approach but gives no stated power figure on the listing.

Buy it if you want to try air frying on a modest budget. Skip it if you bake often.
products.idealFor: Couples and small households trying air fry.
products.skipIf: You regularly cook for four or more.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: An 1800W Cuisinart air fry toaster oven with a smaller footprint for tight kitchens.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven is rated at 1800W and includes air fry, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Its role in this ranking is the compact one: a familiar toaster-oven shape that fits where Breville's units will not.

It places sixth because compactness limits what you can bake in it. A smaller cavity takes fewer pan sizes, and the high wattage helps with fast preheating but cannot compensate for a tight tray. The 1800W rating is among the few figures on offer in this group, which gives you a real number to compare with the toaster oven you may be replacing. Cuisinart's longstanding toaster oven line makes spare parts easy to find.

It is a sensible choice for small kitchens and dorms. Skip it if you want to roast a whole chicken.
pros: Air fry in a familiar format
products.skipIf: You plan to roast whole poultry.

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A larger-capacity Nuwave in the $100 to $200 bracket for busy households.
products.description:
Nuwave pitches the Bravo XL Pro at busier households as an air fryer toaster oven, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Nuwave sells this style of oven on cooking capacity and a long list of preset programs.

It ranks seventh because Nuwave is a younger name in countertop ovens, so long-term parts and service history are shorter than Breville's, Cuisinart's or Ninja's. The oven offers a lot for the money, but check the warranty terms yourself on the listing before buying. Against the Grill Combo version below it costs less and keeps to the core function.

Buy it if you cook for a large family and want capacity at a fair price. Skip it if long-term support is your top concern.
pros: Air fry and oven functions combined
products.idealFor: Large households that cook every day.
products.skipIf: You want a long track record.

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro Air Fryer Toaster Oven w/Grill Combo
products.verdict: The Bravo XL Pro with a grill function, at a higher price.
products.description:
The Grill Combo version of the Bravo XL Pro adds a grill function to the air fryer toaster oven, in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It ranks last because the added grill moves it into Breville's price bracket without matching Breville's track record. A grill setting is useful for searing steaks, melting cheese and browning tops of casseroles, but the standard Bravo XL Pro already covers most of what a household needs. Paying extra for the grill only makes sense if that function is on your regular menu.

It suits cooks who want an indoor grill option and an air fryer in one machine. Skip it if you are happy with the base model.
pros: Air fry and toaster oven combined
Many cooking options in one unit
cons: Costs more than the base Bravo
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a grill and air fry together.

methodology.title: Convection and air-fry capability
methodology.description: We checked which ovens combine a convection fan with a dedicated air fry mode, and which stop at one or the other.

methodology.title: Heat control approach
methodology.description: Smart element systems, digital controls and stated wattage were compared, since steady temperature is what separates a good oven from a toaster with a fan.

methodology.title: Size and fit
methodology.description: Each oven was judged by its footprint class, from compact to XL, against kitchens of different sizes.

methodology.title: Brand support and longevity
methodology.description: Brand history, parts availability and warranty clarity were weighed, because countertop ovens are often used for years.

methodology.title: Value in bracket
methodology.description: Features were set against the $100 to $200 and $200 to $500 price brackets in this guide.

whatMatters.detail: Convection runs a fan to circulate hot air and shorten cooking time. Air fry is a high-fan, high-heat preset, so the two are siblings. When a listing says convection only, as on the Breville BOV845BSS, expect to bake and roast well but not to get the wing-crisp finish of a dedicated mode.

Many cheap ovens switch their elements fully on and off, which swings the actual temperature around your dial setting. Smart element designs, like Breville's, meter the heat more evenly. You cannot always see this on a listing, so look for words like element control and the brand's track record for baking.

Capacity claims mean little if your favorite pan does not fit. Check whether the listing names a pizza or sheet pan it can take, then compare it with the pans you own. XL-class models, such as the Ninja Foodi XL Pro, take wider trays than compact units like the Cuisinart.

Countertop ovens run hot on the outside, and manufacturers ask for open space on the back and sides. A compact footprint helps in a small kitchen, but a cabinet above the oven can trap heat. Measure height as well as width before you buy.

Clear digital or dial controls make a daily-use oven easier to live with. Removable crumb trays and non-stick interiors cut down on scrubbing. Read the listing for these details, since they affect satisfaction more than a long list of preset programs.

howToChoose.subheading: For Replacing a Full-Size Oven Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Even heat control, a cavity that takes your sheet pan, convection and a brand with parts support. Clearance for ventilation matters more than extra presets.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Breville BOV900BSS leads, with the Breville BOV860BSS close behind. The BOV845BSS is the choice if you skip air fry.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You bake weekly, cook for others or want the oven to last. The Breville BOV900BSS and BOV860BSS repay the cost in steadier results.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Use is mostly reheating and frying for one or two. The Ninja Digital or Cuisinart does that for far less.

faq.q: Will a convection toaster oven fit under my cabinets?
faq.a: Check the height on the listing before you buy, and leave a few inches of open space above for heat. XL ovens such as the Breville BOV900BSS and Ninja Foodi XL Pro need the most room. Compact units like the Cuisinart are easier in low-cabinet kitchens.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Paying for presets and ignoring pan fit. A long list of programs matters less than whether the tray takes your pizza or sheet pan. Measure your favorite pan and match it to the stated capacity.

faq.q: Is the Breville worth it over a Ninja?
faq.a: For baking and long-term use, yes. Breville's heat control is steadier and the brand has a long record in this category. If you mostly fry and reheat, the Ninja models do that job well for less.

faq.q: How do I convert recipes for convection?
faq.a: A common rule is to lower the temperature by about 25 degrees Fahrenheit and check food a few minutes early. Some ovens adjust automatically in their presets. Follow the manual if it gives conversion guidance.

faq.q: How do I clean the oven?
faq.a: Unplug it and let it cool, then slide out the crumb tray and wipe the walls down with a damp sponge. Soak removable racks and trays in warm soapy water. Avoid abrasive pads on non-stick surfaces.

faq.q: Can I use foil or parchment inside?
faq.a: Usually yes, but keep it away from the heating elements and weigh it down so the fan does not blow it into them. Check the manual for your model, since air fry modes move air faster than a standard oven.

finalTake: For kitchens that want one oven to do the work of two, the Breville BOV900BSS is the best convection toaster oven here. The Breville BOV860BSS is nearly as capable, and the BOV845BSS suits bakers who skip air fry. For tight counters, the Cuisinart is the smart pick, and the Ninja Digital gives air fry on a modest budget. Check pan fit and clearance before you pay for extra presets.
